name: XP Leveling
description: Tracks experience points and level, computing level-up thresholds from a curve.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.
Upstream module named; no adapter written.

inputs.name: startingXp
inputs.description: Experience already banked toward the next level when this component is constructed. `startingLevel` alone loses everything earned since the last level-up, which matters wherever a run is rebuilt rather than continued — walking into a new region, reloading a save, changing floor. A level and a level-and-a-half are different states and only one of them was expressible.

inputs.name: perLevel
inputs.description: What each level past the first is worth, as named bonuses per level — {meleeDamage: 0.5} is one more damage every two levels. Published summed and floored as `bonuses`, in the shape progression.skills_tree and combat.equipment_slots publish theirs, so combat.melee_basic reads a level the way it reads a sword. Empty, a level is a number on a panel.

inputs.name: xpPerHit
inputs.description: Experience for every blow the player lands. The only source there was: fine for a board where a blow is a turn, wrong for a real-time fight where a quick blade earns more than a killing one and a boss can be farmed for as long as it stands. 0 turns it off.

inputs.name: xpPerKill
inputs.description: Experience for every enemy the player defeats — read off combat.entityDefeated, and only a defeat whose `attacker` is the player's unit (a rat killed by a trap, or the hero's own fall, pays nothing). 0, the default, keeps a build paid by the hit as it always was.

inputs.name: xpByArchetype
inputs.description: Kill experience by what was killed, keyed by the defeat's `archetype` — {rat: 8, boss: 150}. An archetype not named here pays `xpPerKill`.

outputs.name: bonuses
outputs.description: The level's worth, summed: {meleeDamage: 2} at level five with half a point a level. The same named-key shape the skills tree and the equipment slots publish.
